requirement.original: Deep investigation of two problems: AskUserQuestion answer persistence and subagent sidebar missing messages
requirement.clarified: Trace exact data flow for both AskUserQuestion answers and subagent messages end-to-end, identify where data is lost, and document correct fix direction
requirement.what: Fix two data pipeline bugs: (1) AskUserQuestion answers lost on refresh, (2) subagent messages missing from sidebar
requirement.why: Bug #74 and #75 from right sidebar feature - answers show dashes after refresh, sidebar shows incomplete subagent activity

included: Subagent message visibility in sidebar children[]
Both session protocol and JSONL paths
excluded: UI rendering changes in sidebar components

success_criteria: AskUserQuestion answers display correctly after page refresh
All subagent text and tool-call messages appear in sidebar children[]
Fix works for both live streaming and restored/resumed sessions
constraints: ToolCall.permission already has answers? field - use it
Must not break existing permission flow
Must not change server message format

research_findings.reason: Detailed code trace of existing codebase - no external patterns needed

problem_1_askuserquestion.symptom: AskUserQuestion shows dashes instead of selected answers after page refresh
problem_1_askuserquestion.root_cause: Answers are stored ONLY in a module-level Map (permissionAnswersStore in ops.ts) which is lost on refresh. The answers are sent to CLI via RPC, CLI merges them into updatedInput for Claude SDK, but never persists them back to agentState.completedRequests. The tool_result from Claude SDK contains only text output, not the structured answers.
problem_1_askuserquestion.data_flow_break_point: CLI permissionHandler.ts lines 444-466: when moving permission to completedRequests, the answers field from the RPC response is NOT included
problem_1_askuserquestion.secondary_break_point: Claude SDK tool_result does not echo updatedInput.answers back - answers go IN as input but never come OUT as result
problem_1_askuserquestion.fix_direction: Include answers in completedRequests agentState entry (permissionHandler.ts line 444-466). Then in reducer Phase 0 completedRequests processing, copy answers to message.tool.permission.answers. The ToolCall.permission type already has answers? field.

exact_fix_locations.what: In setupClientHandler, when building completedRequests entry, add: answers: message.answers (from the RPC response)
In Phase 0 completedRequests processing, when updating permission fields, also copy completed.answers to message.tool.permission.answers

problem_2_subagent_sidebar.symptom: Subagent sidebar shows incomplete messages - some text and tool calls missing
problem_2_subagent_sidebar.root_cause: The data pipeline for session protocol subagent messages is architecturally correct but has edge cases around message ordering and ID mismatches between permission IDs and CUID2 session subagent IDs

data_flow_analysis.step_1_mapper: sessionProtocolMapper creates tool-call-start with call=CUID2 (for hidden Task tools) and sets subagent=CUID2 on all child envelopes
data_flow_analysis.step_2_normalizer: typesRaw.ts normalizeSessionEnvelope sets parentUUID=envelope.subagent (CUID2), isSidechain=true for all subagent messages
data_flow_analysis.step_3_tracer: reducerTracer registers CUID2 in toolCallToMessageId when processing tool-call-start, then matches subagent messages via toolCallToMessageId.get(parentUuid=CUID2). Orphan buffer handles out-of-order messages.
data_flow_analysis.step_4_reducer: Phase 4 stores sidechain messages in state.sidechains.set(sidechainId, [...]), Phase 4 line 1083-1091 marks parent as changed. convertReducerMessageToMessage line 1199 reads state.sidechains.get(reducerMsg.realID)

potential_issues.issue: Permission ID vs CUID2 mismatch for Task tools
potential_issues.detail: Phase 0 creates permission message with toolIdToMessageId.set(permissionId=toolu_01XYZ, mid). Phase 2 looks up toolIdToMessageId.get(c.id=CUID2) which returns nothing. Creates a SECOND message. Now two messages exist for same tool - one from permission (realID: null), one from tool-call (realID: envelope_id). Phase 4 sidechain lookup matches the second one (correct), but the first one is orphaned in the message list.
potential_issues.fix: In Phase 2, also check toolIdToMessageId by the original tool_use_id (stored in toolUseMap or args). Or in the mapper, use consistent IDs.

potential_issues.issue: Incremental reducer calls miss sidechain updates
potential_issues.detail: If sidechain messages arrive in a later reducer() call than the parent tool-call, Phase 4 correctly adds them to state.sidechains AND marks the parent as changed (line 1083-1091). But this relies on the O(n) scan finding a message with realID matching sidechainId.
potential_issues.fix: Already handled by the Phase 4 changed marking loop

potential_issues.issue: Orphan buffer flushing for session restore
potential_issues.detail: During session restore, all messages arrive at once. If subagent messages appear before their parent tool-call-start in the array, they go into orphan buffer. processOrphans is called when parent is processed (line 190-191). This SHOULD work correctly.
potential_issues.fix: Already handled by orphan buffer mechanism

problem_2_subagent_sidebar.most_likely_root_cause: The duplicate message problem: Phase 0 permission creates message A (realID: null) with toolIdToMessageId key=toolu_01XYZ. Phase 2 creates message B (realID: envelope_id) because CUID2 lookup misses. Sidechains correctly attach to message B. But message A (from permission) may be the one rendered in the main chat if it was created first and has lower createdAt. Message A has no children (its realID is null, so state.sidechains.get(null) returns nothing). Needs browser console verification to confirm.
problem_2_subagent_sidebar.fix_direction: Ensure the tool-call-start message ID (CUID2 for hidden Task tools) is registered in toolIdToMessageId so Phase 2 finds the existing permission message instead of creating a duplicate. OR ensure the permission message gets its realID updated when the tool-call-start arrives. The key is that the message rendered in the chat MUST have a realID that matches the sidechainId used by Phase 4.
